guardian.title: ‘Give him any award, and he’ll come running’: Narendra Modi racks up honours on overseas trips
guardian.description:
Indian prime minister has a habit of collecting awards on his travels, some as their first and only recipient

As Narendra Modi touched down in Seychelles over the weekend, the archipelago nation in the Indian Ocean swiftly bestowed one of its “highest” honours upon the Indian prime minister.

Modi beamed as he accepted the Guardian of the Blue Horizon award from Patrick Herminie, the Seychelles president, complete with a trophy and certificate.

guardian.title: Côte d’Ivoire floods kill 59 as west Africa endures torrential rains
guardian.description:
Authorities say rainy season getting deadlier, with Ghana reporting 13 dead and floods hitting Benin, Togo and Nigeria

Floods in Côte d’Ivoire have killed 59 people since May, the communication minister told a cabinet meeting in Abidjan.

There are fears the toll could further rise as rescue teams continue to search for victims during the rainy season, which runs from May until July, the minister, Amadou Coulibaly, added.

guardian.description:
If we don’t know the source, not only do humans remain at risk but wildlife can suffer needlessly via retaliation

guardian.description:
Report accuses paramilitary force of crimes including ethnic cleansing in systemic campaign against civilians

The Sudanese paramilitary Rapid Support Forces committed crimes against humanity and ethnic cleansing during its campaign to capture El Fasher, Amnesty International has alleged.

guardian.title: ‘Witch-hunt’ in Niger as military regime rounds up LGBTQ+ population
guardian.description:
Fears of resurgence of HIV/Aids amid loss of access to PrEP drugs as at least 40 people arrested in ‘toxic’ climate

A “witch-hunt” is under way in Niger, where dozens of people have been arrested for homosexuality in the west African state following the introduction of a new penal code earlier this year.

Up to 40 people have been arrested and 16 men, including high-ranking military officials, have been imprisoned across the country, according to local media.

guardian.description:
Thousands of volunteers are joined by overseas teams in the hope of finding more survivors in the rubble, reports Tom Phillips in Caraballeda

When twin earthquakes tore through Venezuela’s northern coast last week, Israel Rivas was at home hundreds of miles away in the industrial city of San Félix. guardian.title: Venezuelan man saved from collapsed mall eight days after earthquakes
guardian.description:
Security guard Hernán Alberto Gil Flores, 43, initially told rescuers not to tell his wife in case he did not survive

A 43-year-old security guard who survived last week’s devastating earthquakes in Venezuela thanks to a pocket of air in his workstation cabin has been pulled from the collapsed basement of a shopping centre amid huge cheers from international rescue teams.

guardian.title: Canadian boy dies of rabies after waking to find bat on his face
guardian.description:
Eleven-year-old developed symptoms 19 days after encounter in Ontario in ‘exceedingly rare’ case

Doctors in Canada say a child who awoke to find a bat resting on his nose and mouth while visiting an Ontario cottage later died of rabies, in an “exceedingly rare case” that highlights the need for better public awareness.

In a report published this week in the Canadian Medical Association Journal, infectious disease

guardian.title: Trump refuses to renew US-Canada-Mexico trade pact he once championed
guardian.description:
Trump and US officials opted to keep USMCA alive on short leash of annual reviews rather than longer term renewal

Donald Trump has refused to renew the North American trade pact he once championed as his signature deal, opting instead to keep it alive on a short leash of annual reviews rather than committing to another 16 years.

guardian.description:
• Three of the victims died from suffocation

  • More than a million people gathered in Mexico City

Four people died, three ⁠from suffocation, as thousands of fans crowded Mexico City streets during World Cup celebrations, the capital’s health secretariat ⁠said in the early ⁠hours ​of Wednesday.

The deaths occurred near the Angel of Independence landmark, where thousands of fans had gathered to ⁠celebrate

guardian.title: China says man who flew plane into Beijing skyscraper had mental health problems
guardian.description:
Official statement offers the most detailed official account yet of the highly unusual and fatal incident in Beijing

Chinese authorities said the man who flew a small plane into Beijing’s tallest skyscraper last week was a 66-year-old who had mental health problems.

The statement published on Thursday offered the most detailed official account yet of the highly unusual incident that occurred in Beijing’s central business district on the evening of 26 June.

guardian.title: At least nine monks killed in Thailand after boy drives truck into procession
guardian.description:
Charges yet to be filed over incident in Mukdahan involving 11-year-old, as police seek to establish circumstances

An 11-year-old boy has driven his parents’ truck into a Buddhist procession in Thailand, killing at least nine monks.

CCTV footage shared by a local rescue group showed the moment the monks, wearing orange robes, were run over as they walked in procession along a road. The timestamp on the footage was shortly before 11am local time on Thursday.

guardian.title: Papua separatists kill American pilot in ‘message’ to US and Indonesia
guardian.description:
Rebels shoot pilot and set his civilian ⁠plane on fire amid long-running low-level battle for independence in region

Separatist rebels in Indonesia’s restive easternmost region of Papua have shot dead an American pilot and set a civilian ⁠plane on fire, in what a spokesperson for a local militant group described as a “message” to the US and Indonesian governments.

guardian.title: Young Indonesian couple publicly caned after kissing on TikTok
guardian.description:
Unmarried man and woman whipped 21 times each because they had violated province’s version of Islamic law

A young couple in Indonesia’s conservative Aceh province have been publicly caned after a Sharia court convicted them of violating Islamic law by kissing during a TikTok livestream.

guardian.description:
Law comes into effect that critics fear will further erode rights of Uyghurs and Tibetans, as well as allow Beijing to pursue dissidents abroad

A new ethnic unity law has come into effect in China despite warnings from Taiwan, the United Nations and rights groups that it could threaten freedoms, especially for minorities.

rfi.title: El Nino set to be 'strong' as UN warns of heatwaves and floods
rfi.description: El Nino is here and will quickly develop into a strong event between July and September, fuelling the likelihood of extreme weather, the United Nations' climate agency warned Friday.

rfi.title: DRC trials experimental treatment for rare Ebola strain as outbreak worsens
rfi.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo has launched a clinical trial of experimental Ebola treatments as the outbreak continues to spread in the north-east of the country.

rfi.title: As Sahel states withdraw from ICC, NGOs warn of ‘impunity’ over war crimes
rfi.description: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger have initiated a year-long process of withdrawing from the International Criminal Court, a move human rights defenders say will leave victims of war crimes without access to justice.

rfi.title: France reports sharp rise in deaths after record June heatwave
rfi.description: France recorded a rise of nearly 30 percent in deaths during the week beginning 22 June, the peak of the country's record-breaking heatwave, the public health authority said on Friday.

rfi.title: Hunt for Ukrainian woman after Monaco bomb attack targeting sanctioned tycoon
rfi.description: Interpol have issued a worldwide alert over a Ukrainian woman suspected of planting a bomb in Monaco that injured three people, including a tycoon of Ukrainian origin.

rfi.title: Belgium opens up Congo archives amid global minerals race
rfi.description: From century-old maps to meticulous field notes, Belgium is sitting on a trove of geological records on colonial-era Congo – a coveted archive it is working to open up amid a global scramble for critical minerals.

rfi.title: Switzerland beat Algeria 2-0 to move into World Cup last 16
rfi.description: Breel Embolo scored in the first half, Dan Ndoye tallied at the start of the second half and Switzerland advanced to the World Cup's round of 16 with a 2-0 victory over Algeria on Thursday night in Vancouver.

rfi.title: US shows ‘increasingly blatant’ bias over DRC peace deal, says Rwandan minister
rfi.description: The fragile peace process between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo is under renewed pressure, as the United States imposes fresh sanctions over alleged links to mineral trafficking from areas controlled by M23 rebels. Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe tells RFI Kigali is being unfairly blamed – arguing that the Congolese government has failed to meet its own commitments under the US-brokered peace deal.

rfi.title: Wildfires spread across southern France, as heatwave reignites forest concerns
rfi.description: Wildfires have broken out across southern France, forcing evacuations and stretching firefighting teams as the country prepares for the third heatwave of the summer, with the country's forests under increasing threat from climate change and disputes over logging.

rfi.title: World Bank drops climate funding target, raising fears for Africa
rfi.description: The World Bank has abandoned its target of directing 45 percent of its financing to projects that help tackle climate change, prompting warnings that poorer countries – especially in Africa – could receive less support to adapt to a warming world.

rfi.title: Paris death penalty congress warns abolition cannot be taken for granted
rfi.description: The fight to abolish the death penalty remains "eminently contemporary", French President Emmanuel Macron said as campaigners, judges and former death row prisoners gathered in Paris this week for the World Congress Against the Death Penalty, amid rising executions worldwide and renewed support for capital punishment in some democracies.

rfi.title: Podcast: Adapting to heat, France's fitness boom, Paris Mosque at 100
rfi.description: As France's record-breaking heatwave last week raises questions about how the country will have to adapt to a warming climate, we look at what that could mean for French culture. We also explore the country's growing interest in fitness – driven in part by its most popular YouTuber – and examine how the Grand Mosque of Paris, which marks its centenary this year, became both a symbol of Islam in France and a recurring source of political tension.

rfi.title: Senegal midfielder Gueye refuses to play while coaching staff stay in charge
rfi.description: Senegal midfielder Pape Gueye announced he will not play any more international games for his country while the squad's coaching staff remains in charge.

rfi.title: Google loses final appeal against EU’s record €4.1bn anti-trust fine
rfi.description: The European Union’s top court has dismissed Google’s final appeal against a record €4.1 billion anti-trust fine, confirming one of Brussels’ most significant victories in its long-running effort to rein in Big Tech.

rfi.title: Ramos strikes late to take Portugal past Croatia into last-16 at World Cup
rfi.description: Gonçalo Ramos scored a stoppage time winner to send Portugal past Croatia into a last 16 showdown with Spain.

rfi.title: Algeria votes in parliamentary elections amid public apathy and football fever
rfi.description: Algerians are voting in parliamentary elections on Thursday, with cost of living concerns, questions over political freedoms and the national football team’s World Cup run all competing for public attention.

rfi.title: France confirms dates for 2027 presidential election
rfi.description: France will hold the first round of its next presidential election on 18 April 2027 and the runoff on 2 May after the government formally approved the dates at Wednesday's cabinet meeting.

rfi.title: France advances assisted dying law with strict rules and safeguards
rfi.description: France's National Assembly has approved a new version of a bill creating a legal right to assisted dying, bringing the country closer to a major change in end-of-life care. The legislation sets out who could qualify, how requests would be made and the safeguards designed to prevent abuse of the law.

euronews.description: Six Russian scientists linked to Alexei Navalny's epibatidine poisoning now face asset freezes and EU-wide travel bans.

euronews.title: Humanoid robots showcase football skills
euronews.description: Humanoid robots compete in football matches at RoboCup in Incheon, South Korea, showcasing advances in robotics as spectators watch the action.

euronews.description: Pakistan’s President Asif Ali Zardari expressed sorrow over the crash, offered condolences to the families of those killed and wished the injured a speedy recovery.

euronews.title: Ukraine to call on NATO partners to deliver air defence after brutal Russian bombardment
euronews.description: Ukraine is calling on its partners to deliver air defence systems to Ukraine after a Russian aerial attack killed at least 30 people on 2 July. With NATO allies preparing to meet in Ankara, Kyiv is urging them not to delay what they have already promised.

euronews.title: The ‘Wonderwall’ effect: Have England finally got a decent World Cup anthem?
euronews.description: The team's travelling football supporters have taken to singing ‘Wonderwall’ by Oasis with the players at full-time. Now, streams are up and a new tradition is born. Can it last?

euronews.description: As Germany prepares to permanently station 5,000 troops in Lithuania, one schoolgirl has already experienced the country's future brigade firsthand after winning a ride in a Bundeswehr tank.

euronews.title: A year with zero deaths on its streets:  How Helsinki became a world reference for road safety
euronews.description: With around 1.4 million inhabitants, the Helsinki metropolitan area has achieved an unquestionable milestone in road safety. What can other EU capitals and big cities learn from its success story?

euronews.title: Lagarde mulls leaving ECB early to play a role in French elections
euronews.description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said she is considering the possibility of taking part in the upcoming French elections, a move that could result in her stepping down from her post earlier than planned.

euronews.title: Iran to host dozens of foreign leaders for Khamenei's funeral, with Western nations absent
euronews.description: Russia's Medvedev, Pakistan's prime minister and Taliban officials are among roughly 30 country delegations expected as Iran buries slain Ayatollah Ali Khamenei this week.

euronews.description: The alert says Berezovska speaks German, has dark hair, and has a tattoo - possibly of a snake - on her upper right arm.

euronews.description: Tripadvisor's new AI review summaries are masking reports of food poisoning, sexual harassment and serious hygiene failures, a Which? investigation has found.

euronews.title: Amazon set to launch Leo, its rival to SpaceX's Starlink internet, later this year
euronews.description: Amazon has deployed enough satellites to begin offering its Leo internet service this year, marking its most significant step yet in the race to take on SpaceX's Starlink.

euronews.title: Ukraine and Moldova set to open another cluster of EU accession talks
euronews.description: EU countries have unanimously agreed to start the process to open another accession cluster with Ukraine and Moldova, the one on external relations, with a formal ceremony expected on 14 July.

euronews.title: What is GLM 5.2? The new Chinese AI model that’s rivalling Anthropic
euronews.description: China's GLM-5.2 rivals Claude and GPT-5.5 and was released a day after the US export ban on Anthropic models.

euronews.title: October deadline for China talks 'not realistic at all', chief trade MEP says
euronews.description: Bernd Lange, head of the European Parliament's trade committee, told Euronews the EU should be pushing China hard on unfair industrial subsidies and other pressing issues.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, incendies dans le sud de la France : le ministre de l’intérieur, Laurent Nuñez, se dit « très inquiet pour la saison » et appelle à la vigilance
lemonde.description: « On a un mois d’avance sur les départs de feu », a dit le ministre à l’occasion d’un déplacement dans l’Aude, un des six départements du sud de la France placés en « danger très élevé » par Météo-France. L’incendie le plus important est actif depuis mercredi dans la zone de Pouzols-Minervois.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : dans la ville de Kiev, au lendemain de l’attaque la plus meurtrière depuis le début de la guerre, les recherches se poursuivent dans les décombres
lemonde.description: Au moins 30 personnes ont été tuées à Kiev dans l’attaque menée jeudi par l’armée russe, selon un bilan fourni vendredi par les secouristes.

lemonde.title: Sénatoriales 2026 : une répartition des sièges de moins en moins représentative de la démographie française
lemonde.description: Une partie des 348 sièges de la chambre haute est remise en jeu en septembre. Fondée sur le recensement de 1999, la carte des sénatoriales favorise, en nombre d’élus, Paris et les départements ruraux au détriment des territoires qui gagnent aujourd’hui des habitants.

lemonde.title: GPA : la France doit reconnaître la filiation actée par un tribunal étranger, décide la Cour de cassation
lemonde.description: La Cour a examiné la situation d’un couple d’hommes français vivant au Canada, ayant eu recours à deux reprises à une GPA dans ce pays où elle est légale.

lemonde.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : Kansas City, nouvelle « capitale » du « soccer » aux Etats-Unis
lemonde.description: La ville du Midwest accueille six matchs du Mondial, dont un quart de finale. Elle a su se tailler une place à part sur l’échiquier du football aux Etats-Unis, grâce notamment à ses infrastructures et à la vitalité de ses clubs.

lemonde.title: « Le remplacement des journalistes secrétaires de rédaction par une IA à “La Gazette des communes” met en péril la qualité éditoriale du titre »
lemonde.description: Un collectif de lecteurs du magazine spécialisé dans les métiers de la fonction publique territoriale, constitué d’élus, d’anciens ministres, de responsables associatifs, appelle, dans une tribune au « Monde », le groupe à renoncer au plan social afin de conserver « ce qui fait sa valeur essentielle : le discernement humain ».

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : le RN étoffe son équipe de campagne, avec notamment la nièce de Marine Le Pen
lemonde.description: Le Rassemblement national a dévoilé vendredi les noms de nouveaux membres de son équipe de campagne pour la présidentielle, dont celui de Nolwenn Olivier, qui sera la directrice de la communication.

lemonde.title: Tentative d’assassinat à Monaco : une femme ukrainienne recherchée par Interpol ; les faits « semblent indiquer » que la suspecte « n’a pas agi seule », selon le parquet
lemonde.description: La suspecte, dont le « dernier domicile connu » est en Allemagne, a pris la fuite via la France puis l’Italie dans une voiture de location.

lemonde.title: Jimmy Mohamed, animateur du « Mag de la santé », mis en retrait temporairement de France Télévisions
lemonde.description: La femme du médecin a publié sur Instagram des photos d’elle avec des hématomes sur les bras, remontant à décembre dernier selon ses dires. « Je n’ai jamais exercé de violences », a assuré le médecin, vendredi, sur le même réseau social.

lemonde.title: « Sans investisseurs, les nouveaux venus finissent par couler » : face à Instagram ou TikTok, la difficile survie des plateformes européennes
lemonde.description: Comment concurrencer les réseaux américains ou chinois ? De nombreuses aventures ont jusqu’ici mené à des échecs ou à des succès mineurs. Mais alors que l’on parle plus que jamais de souveraineté numérique, des initiatives continuent à voir le jour, en quête d’appui des pouvoirs publics.

lemonde.title: Orthographe au bac : le discours de fermeté du ministre n’a guère modifié les consignes de correction
lemonde.description: Selon les témoignages et documents recueillis par « Le Monde », le tour de vis voulu par Edouard Geffray s’est traduit de façon très inégale selon les académies, les disciplines et les inspecteurs. Les enseignants estiment déjà prendre en compte la maîtrise de la langue dans leur évaluation.

lemonde.title: En Occitanie, la campagne d’arrachage des vignes bat son plein : « Si on regarde le paysage, ça fait peur »
lemonde.description: Pour la deuxième année, plus de 28 000 hectares de vignes seront arrachés en France, contre indemnisation pour les viticulteurs. Dans l’Aude et les Pyrénées-Orientales, la mesure redessine les paysages et les pratiques.

lemonde.title: Les Etats-Unis retirent une grande partie de leurs soldats du Nigeria, mais maintiennent le partage de renseignements
lemonde.description: L’armée américaine, en coordination avec les autorités nigérianes, a procédé à plusieurs frappes aériennes dans le pays contre l’insurrection djihadiste ces derniers mois.

lemonde.title: Pourquoi la plateforme de crowdfunding immobilier Bricks veut racheter une banque
lemonde.description: La société prévoit de débourser 30 millions d’euros pour profiter de l’agrément d’un établissement étranger. Elle espère ainsi se lancer dans le crédit immobilier en s’appuyant sur sa base de clients.

lemonde.title: Présidentielles au Pérou et en Colombie : le vote des expatriés a favorisé la victoire de l’extrême droite
lemonde.description: Les Péruviens de l’étranger ont permis l’élection de Keiko Fujimori, minoritaire chez les résidants de son pays. Sans avoir été décisifs, les Colombiens expatriés ont largement privilégié Abelardo de la Espriella.

lemonde.title: Dominique Boutonnat, ex-patron du CNC jugé en appel pour une agression sexuelle sur son filleul, a été relaxé
lemonde.description: Le parquet général avait requis trois ans de prison dont un ferme, la même peine qu’en première instance, soulignant la « posture de déni » de Dominique Boutonnat.

lemonde.title: Soudan : alerte rouge de l’ONU face à la « catastrophe » d’El-Obeid
lemonde.description: Depuis plusieurs jours, l’ONU, des ONG et divers gouvernements s’inquiètent d’une possible attaque imminente à El-Obeid, grande ville du Soudan assiégée par les paramilitaires. Ils redoutent des déplacements de centaines de milliers de personnes.

lemonde.title: Festival d’Aix-en-Provence : avec « Accabadora », le compositeur Francesco Filidei entretient le cœur vibrant de l’opéra
lemonde.description: L’Italien connu pour ses explorations bruitistes s’emploie « à faire chanter des choses qui chantent déjà toutes seules ».

zeit.title: Welternährungsprogramm der Vereinten Nationen: »Wir erwarten, dass noch sehr viel mehr Menschen hungern werden«
zeit.description: Carl Skau, amtierender Exekutivdirektor des Welternährungsprogramms, spricht über globale Folgen des Irankriegs – und über humanitäre Hilfe unter unmöglichen Bedingungen.

zeit.description: Demos, Blockaden, Konzerte: Der AfD-Parteitag in Erfurt am Wochenende ist für die Polizei ein Großeinsatz. Tausende Beamte sind vor Ort, es gibt Straßensperrungen.

zeit.description: Es heißt, die Mehrheit lehne Reformen ab, sobald sie selbst betroffen ist. Doch auch harte Einschnitte können akzeptiert werden. Entscheidend ist etwas anderes.

zeit.description: Knapp 40.000 Menschen haben in Deutschland im ersten Halbjahr einen Erstantrag auf Asyl gestellt. Das war mehr als ein Drittel weniger als noch ein Jahr zuvor.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : les opérations de secours se poursuivent à Kiev dans un air pollué
france24fr.description: Alors que le bilan des frappes russes sur Kiev dans la nuit de mercredi à jeudi s'élève désormais à 30 morts et près de 100 blessés, les secouristes continuent vendredi leurs recherches dans les décombres. La capitale ukrainienne est enveloppée de fumée et les services de la municipalité ont signalé une dégradation de la qualité de l'air.

france24fr.title: Ils vivent sans climatisation et sont au frais même lors des canicules
france24fr.description: La clim' n'est pas la seule solution contre les canicules. Ces habitants d'une résidence à Montpellier ont presque froid alors qu'il fait plus de 30 degrés dehors. Pourtant, aucun n'a de climatiseur. Façades ondulées pour accentuer le vent, balcons inspirés de l'architecture arabe... les adaptations climatiques sont efficaces contre les fortes chaleurs, et bien plus durables.

france24fr.title: Municipales : comment une campagne de désinformation inédite a été menée depuis Israël contre LFI
france24fr.description: Polémiques artificielles, fausses accusations... Plusieurs opérations de désinformation ont visé les municipales de 2026 en France, selon l'enquête de Viginum, le service de lutte contre les ingérences numériques étrangères. Une campagne inédite, menée depuis Israël, a notamment ciblé La France insoumise.

france24fr.title: Et si notre réalité n'était qu'un gigantesque bug informatique ?
france24fr.description: Imaginez que notre univers ne soit qu'un gigantesque jeu vidéo. Popularisée par "Matrix" et tournée en dérision dans "Le Vertige" – la dernière comédie de Quentin Dupieux –, cette idée est prise au sérieux par des figures de la tech tels Elon Musk, Sam Altman ou encore George Hotz. Lors de sa conférence au festival SXSW intitulée "Jailbreaking the Simulation", ce hacker expliquait rechercher des failles ("glitchs") dans notre quotidien. Il milite pour trouver ces vulnérabilités, prendre le contr

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : altercation entre la police et la délégation égyptienne à Dallas
france24fr.description: Une altercation a éclaté dans le hall de l’hôtel de la sélection égyptienne à Dallas, à la veille de son 16e de finale de Coupe du monde face à l’Australie. Selon des vidéos diffusées sur les réseaux sociaux, un jeune supporter égyptien a tenté de prendre une photo avec Mahmoud Hassan Trezeguet, avant d’être stoppé par un agent de sécurité. Cette intervention a provoqué une montée de tension, impliquant plusieurs membres du staff, dont le sélectionneur Hossam Hassan et son adjoint Ibrahim Hassan

france24fr.title: Soudan : El-Obeid, ville clé du conflit, sous tension mais résistante
france24fr.description: Roland Marchal, chercheur au Centre de recherches internationales de Sciences Po et spécialiste de l’Afrique, était l’invité de France 24 pour évoquer la situation des civils au Soudan, en particulier à El-Obeid, ville assiégée qui retient l’attention de l’ONU. Alors que les Forces de soutien rapide poursuivent leur progression vers l’est dans une guerre qui dure depuis trois ans et disposent notamment de drones dans les combats autour de la ville, le chercheur estime toutefois peu crédible un s

france24fr.title: "Malédiction" de la 86e minute, Mbappé dictateur : la Coupe du monde vue des réseaux sociaux
france24fr.description: Le Mondial 2026 de football se joue aussi... sur les réseaux sociaux ! Retour en images sur ce qui a fait parler sur les plateformes cette semaine avec Valentin Cacheux.

france24fr.title: Iran : journée de recueillement pour les funérailles du guide suprême Ali Khamenei
france24fr.description: Des milliers de personnes sont attendues sur plusieurs jours pour les cérémonies de funérailles du guide suprême iranien Ali Khamenei, annoncé mort à la suite de frappes américaines intervenues le 28 février. Le début du recueillement a lieu aujourd’hui, dans un climat de forte émotion et de tensions autour des enjeux politiques et sécuritaires. Les détails avec l’envoyé spécial de France 24 sur place, Abdallah Malkawi.

france24fr.title: Venezuela : l’espoir de retrouver des survivants s’amenuise après le double séisme meurtrier
france24fr.description: Huit jours après le double séisme qui a frappé le Venezuela, les chances de retrouver des survivants s’amenuisent alors que le bilan dépasse les 2 600 morts et que des dizaines de milliers de personnes sont toujours portées disparues. Dans les zones sinistrées, les secours poursuivent les recherches au milieu des décombres et des scènes de désolation, tandis que les autorités sont critiquées pour la lenteur de la réponse face à une crise humanitaire qui pourrait encore s’aggraver.

france24fr.title: Tour de France 2026 : les cinq étapes clés à surveiller
france24fr.description: Il est temps, le Tour de France 2026 sera lancé samedi à Barcelone. Parmi les 21 étapes, cinq pourraient faire basculer l'issue du Tour.

france24fr.title: Pourquoi malgré la fin des importations depuis le Niger, le nucléaire français ne manque pas d’uranium
france24fr.description: Des internautes et la télévision publique nigérienne affirment que les centrales nucléaires françaises manqueraient d’uranium en raison de la fin des importations en provenance du Niger. C’est inexact : la France a diversifié ses fournisseurs et ses stocks stratégiques lui permettraient d'alimenter ces centrales pendant plusieurs années.

france24fr.title: Canicule en France : plus de 7000 départs de feu dans le sud
france24fr.description: Après une nuit de lutte contre les flammes, l'incendie de Lançon-Provence est désormais fixé. Si les habitations ont pu être préservées, plusieurs centaines de personnes ont dû être évacuées en urgence à La Fare-les-Oliviers, et les secours restent mobilisés face à un risque de reprise. Dans le sud de la France, plus de 7000 départs de feu ont été comptabilisés.

france24fr.title: "Les échappées de Kaboul" : retour sur l'exfiltration secrète des cyclistes afghanes
france24fr.description: Dans "Actuelles", nous revenons sur une incroyable histoire : celle de l'exfiltration de l'équipe féminine de cyclisme afghane en septembre 2021, un peu plus d'un mois après la prise de contrôle de Kaboul par les Taliban. Parmi la quarantaine de femmes cyclistes évacuées, Wahida et Nazanin. Elles reviennent sur leur parcours, cinq ans après avoir fui leur pays.

france24fr.title: Soudan : risque d’attaque imminente à El-Obeid, alerte l'ONU
france24fr.description: Le Conseil des droits de l’homme de l’ONU s’est réuni en urgence pour évoquer le risque d’une attaque imminente des Forces de soutien rapide contre la ville assiégée d’El-Obeid, au Soudan. Dans un pays ravagé par plus de trois ans de guerre entre l’armée et les FSR, les combats ont déjà fait des dizaines de milliers de morts et déplacé près de 12 millions de personnes, et les ONG alertent sur des exactions et des accusations de crimes graves.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l’Algérie sort par la petite porte
france24fr.description: Les Fennecs ont été éliminés en 16èmes de finale par la Suisse (2-0). Après le match, le capitaine Riyad Mahrez a annoncé sa retraite internationale. De son côté le Portugal renverse la Croatie (2-1). Les Portugais ont d’abord souffert avant de passer devant les Croates dans les arrêts de jeu. Ils affronteront la Roja en 8èmes. Les Espagnols, eux, ont largement dominé l’Autriche (3-0). Ils ont pu profiter d’un doublé de Mikel Oyarzabal, et d’un magnifique but de la tête de Pedro Porro.

france24fr.title: Madonna la joue électro avec son nouvel album Confessions II
france24fr.description: La reine de la pop a sorti vendredi son quinzième album, "Confessions II". Dans un registre inattendu, elle se lance avec cette réponse à son album mythique "Confessions on a dance floor", dans des sonorités électro et réaffirme son rejet du système.

france24fr.title: Législatives en Algérie : la participation au cœur des enjeux du scrutin
france24fr.description: Élections législatives en Algérie. Les Algériens étaient appelés aux urnes ce jeudi pour renouveler le Parlement. Mais plus que la répartition des sièges, c'est le niveau de participation qui concentre toutes les attentions, sur fond de risque d'abstention élevée. Les premières estimations laissent entrevoir une mobilisation limitée.

france24fr.title: Kylian Mbappé en dictateur Mobutu : quand les Bleus s’emparent de la trend
france24fr.description:
#Mondial2026 : sur les réseaux sociaux, les images générées par IA de Kylian Mbappé habillé en dictateur et donnant des ordres à son équipe et aux arbitres pullulent. 
 
Au point que ses coéquipiers se sont moqués de cette tendance en surnommant le capitaine des Bleus ‘Mobut’, comme Mobutu, le dictateur du Zaïre.

nzz.title: Anschlag in Monaco: Eine Paketbombe verletzt den ukrainischen Geschäftsmann Wadim Jermolajew
nzz.description: Drei Ukrainer sind in Monaco durch eine Paketbombe verletzt worden. Unter den Opfern befindet sich ein Unternehmer, der seit Ende 2023 auf der Sanktionsliste Kiews steht. Die Behörden verdächtigen eine Ukrainerin mit Wohnsitz in Deutschland.

nzz.title: «Switzerland – great since 1291»: Guy Parmelins Maga-Mütze sorgt für Aufregung
nzz.description: Wer in der Schweiz heute als Politiker Erfolg haben will, der setzt sich am besten ein Schmuckstück auf den Kopf. Über den Hut als Statement

nzz.description: Donald Trump will der Hauptstadt seinen Stempel aufdrücken. Mit viel Marmor, vielen Säulen und vor allem viel Gold. Aber Washington ist keine gewöhnliche Stadt – sie ist ein architektonisches Sinnbild der amerikanischen Demokratie.

nzz.title: Effizient, abgezockt, reif: Nach dem starken Auftritt gegen Algerien dürfen die Schweizer Fussballer vom WM-Viertelfinal träumen
nzz.description: Das Team von Murat Yakin zeigt beim 2:0 im Sechzehntelfinal seine ganze Klasse und Erfahrung – so könnte es an der WM weit gehen. Und selbst der Bundespräsident Guy Parmelin hat in Vancouver einen starken Auftritt.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Von Marilyn bis Malcolm X – neun amerikanische Bild-Ikonen, die Sie vielleicht noch nicht kennen
nzz.description: Anlässlich des 250. Jahrestages der Gründung der USA erzählen wir die Geschichten dieser Bilder und der Fotografen dahinter.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Thailand muss Frauen und Kinder besser schützen
nzz.description: Hunderttausende Sextouristen besuchen jährlich ein Land, in dem Prostitution eigentlich illegal ist. Thailands Regierung, Polizei und Behörden dulden sie, weil es ein profitables Geschäft ist. Der jüngste Mord an einer 17-Jährigen zeigt, wohin diese Heuchelei führt.

nzz.title: Fensterlos durch die Nacht: Taylor Swift und Travis Kelce feiern vermutlich die Hochzeit des Jahrtausends
nzz.description: Im Madison Square Garden steigt am Freitag die Party mit rund 1000 Gästen. Wer nicht dabei ist, wie hoch der Romantikfaktor ist und was das Datum mit Trump zu tun haben könnte.

nzz.title: Eine wundersame Wiedergeburt: Dank Teheran schöpft der Hizbullah in Libanon wieder Hoffnung
nzz.description: Die in letzter Zeit schwer angeschlagene Schiitenmiliz gibt sich wieder selbstbewusst und droht der Regierung in Beirut sogar mit einem Putsch. Aber wie stark ist die von Iran unterstützte Truppe wirklich?

nzz.title: Der Supreme Court spielt «Hau den Maulwurf» mit Trump, verfolgt aber eine eigene eingreifende Agenda
nzz.description: Der Oberste Gerichtshof der USA hat die Macht der Exekutive stark ausgebaut – was nebenbei den Republikanern an der Wahlurne helfen wird. Doch der Kurs der Konservativen ist ideologisch motiviert, wohl weniger parteipolitisch.

nzz.title: Leben aus dem Labor: Eine Forscherin präsentiert die weltweit erste künstliche Zelle und provoziert die Fachwelt
nzz.description: Es könnte der Beginn eines neuen Zeitalters der synthetischen Biologie sein. Doch der Wissenschafterin geht es offenbar vor allem darum, schnell Millionen Dollar für ihre nächsten Pläne einzusammeln.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Erdbeben in Venezuela: Anzahl Opfer steigt auf 2595 +++ Millionen-Fonds für den Wiederaufbau geplant
nzz.description: Innerhalb weniger Minuten richteten zwei Erdbeben in Venezuela verheerende Schäden an. Rettungskräfte suchen unter den Trümmern nach Überlebenden. Über das Ausmass der Schäden ist wenig bekannt.

nzz.title: Gegen Algerien spielte die Schweiz an der WM erstmals reif – diese Grafiken zeigen ihre Effizienz und einen Schlüssel zum Erfolg
nzz.description: Der Schweizer Equipe gelingt der erste Sieg in einer WM-K.-o.-Runde seit 1938. Und: die erste rundum überzeugende Vorstellung im laufenden Turnier. Eine visuelle Analyse.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Hitze in Europa: Der Schnee auf den Schweizer Gletschern schmilzt früh +++ In Frankreich wüten heftige Waldbrände
nzz.description: Wo ist es gerade besonders heiss? Und was sind die Auswirkungen auf die Menschen und die Umwelt? Hier finden Sie die neuesten Meldungen zu Hitzerekorden, Dürren und Bränden in Europa.

nzz.title: Julian Nagelsmann tritt als deutscher Nationaltrainer zurück
nzz.description: Es hat sich nach dem WM-Aus gegen Paraguay abgezeichnet, jetzt steht fest: Julian Nagelsmann tritt ab. Als Nachfolge-Topkandidat gilt Jürgen Klopp.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Polizei-News aus Zürich: Protestcamp gegen Datencenter in Benken wird geräumt
nzz.description: Die neuesten Polizeimeldungen aus der Region.

observador.title: Tecnologia no Mundial garante a verdade desportiva
observador.description: Pedro Henriques elogia o sensor IMU e o fora de jogo semiautomático que anulou o golo da Croácia. Esclarece ainda que a Lei Prestianni não é aplicável a conversas amigáveis.

observador.title: As notícias das 15h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: O outro chip que Portugal precisa para passar a Espanha
observador.description: Golo anulado à Croácia aos 90+13' foi a janela de oportunidade para reviravolta de Portugal abrir a porta aos oitavos. Segue-se a campeã europeia Espanha, sem fazer sala e a valer uma ida aos quartos.

observador.title: Perda da nacionalidade cai. Chega chumba proposta do PSD
observador.description: PSD não convenceu Chega com nova proposta que acomodava observações do Tribunal Constitucional, e recusou comprar uma guerra reconfirmando o decreto com inconstitucionalidades.

observador.title: Chega diz-se "de esquerda" na redução da idade da reforma
observador.description: O partido reiterou a defesa da redução da idade de reforma para os 65 anos e, às acusações de que estaria alinhado com partidos como PCP e BE, respondeu que nesta matéria se assume "de esquerda".

observador.title: PS quer que ministro resolva problemas dos exames nacionais
observador.description: Após adiamento da 2.ª fase dos exames por falhas informáticas, o PS critica o "estado de negação" do ministro da Educação e espera que correção ao calendário "seja a última".

observador.title: MNE manifesta "profundo pesar" pela morte de João Felgueiras
observador.description: "A sua vida marcada pela generosidade, entrega e fé foi reconhecida por condecorações do Estado português e timorense" recorda o MNE, expressando "respeito e gratidão" à memória do padre jesuíta.

observador.title: Cinco arguidos por burla em Coimbra, Guarda e Porto
observador.description: Foram constituídos arguidos cinco pessoas, entre os 29 e 73 anos. A apreensão contou com vários documentos, mais de 4 mil euros em dinheiro, vários telemóveis e "diverso material informático".

observador.title: PS saúda normalidade institucional com eleição de Luísa Neto
observador.description: Candidata obteve os dois terços necessários após falhar em junho. PS fala em "normalidade institucional" e nota que a maioria não passa pelo Chega.

observador.title: Escolas não sabem se afixarão notas na nova data
observador.description: "O ministro admitiu que este projeto não começou bem. Eu diria que começo mal e continua mal. Ainda há muitos ajustes para fazer", diz Filinto Lima, da associação de diretores das escolas.

observador.title: Seguro promete empenho na CPLP
observador.description: O Presidente da República defendeu que a organização não pode "perder o norte" e tem de promover, dentro e fora, os seus valores fundadores. Seguro assumiu estas posições numa visita à sede da CPLP.

observador.title: Parlamento manifesta pesar por antigo deputado socialista
observador.description: No texto do voto, os deputados socialistas lamentam a morte de Francisco Fonenga, antigo deputado, e destacam a "dedicação à causa pública" e a "marca indelével na sua terra natal, Campo Maior".

observador.title: Ventura pede regresso de PM e "puxão de orelhas" a ministro
observador.description: Para o presidente do Chega, depois de Luís Montenegro estar presente no Canadá a acompanhar a Seleção Nacional de futebol, é preciso que o chefe do Executivo "volte para Portugal".

observador.title: CGTP manifesta-se junto ao Conselho de Ministros
observador.description: A central sindical, representada por cerca de meia centena de manifestantes em Guimarães, concentrou-se junto ao local onde vai decorrer o Conselho de Ministros.

observador.title: 14h. Vouzela. MAI não exclui a hipótese de fogo posto
observador.description: Luís Neves acredita que as próximas horas vão trazer condições mais favoráveis para o combate às chamas. Ainda, Ventura pede ao PM que volte para Portugal para coordenar o combate aos fogos.

observador.title: Casal indonésio açoitado por partilhar beijo no TikTok
observador.description: Uma jovem de 25 anos, e um jovem, de 22 anos, foram chicoteados 21 vezes em praça pública, por se terem beijado sem serem casados. O tribunal considerou o ato uma violação da lei islâmica local.

observador.title: A história contra quem voa: a feroz concorrência de Pogacar
observador.description: A 113.ª Volta a França promete ser das mais renhidas de sempre... à partida. Pogacar vai em busca da quinta vitória frente a um Vingegaard ao nível dos melhores tempos. Seixas e Del Toro estreiam-se.

observador.title: Dependência do jogo é risco para a China, afirma estudo
observador.description: O estudo, publicado na Universidade Politécnica de Macau, conclui que, embora o jogo e o turismo tenham aumentado o crescimento económico, também ameaçaram a segurança financeira nacional.

spiegel.title: Penélope Cruz will Führerschein machen
spiegel.description: Bislang war Penélope Cruz als Passenger Princess unterwegs. Nun überlegt die Schauspielerin, doch noch den Führerschein zu machen – mit 52. Schuld daran ist U2-Sänger Bono.

spiegel.title: Stade: Kinder nach Tat von Stade Vollwaisen – mehr als 600.000 Euro Spenden
spiegel.description: Durch die Schüsse in Stade sollen zwei Kleinkinder zu Vollwaisen geworden sein: ihr Vater starb wohl bereits im April, ihre Mutter wurde bei der Tat getötet, hieß es auf einer Spendenplattform. Die Höhe der Spenden ist ungewöhnlich.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 heute: Das sollten Sie vor den Spielen am Abend und in der Nacht wissen
spiegel.description: Ägypten hat eine historische Chance, Argentinien trifft auf einen krassen Außenseiter. Und: Kolumbien hofft auf Luis Díaz. Alles Wichtige zu den Partien des Tages erfahren Sie hier.

spiegel.title: Heftige Kritik an geplanter Einschränkung der Informationsfreiheit
spiegel.description: Union und SPD wollen das Land modernisieren. Beschlossen wurde aber auch die Reform des Informationsfreiheitsgesetzes. Kritiker sehen einen »krassen Rückschritt« und fürchten den Verlust »mühsam erkämpfter Bürgerrechte«.

spiegel.title: Russlands Angriffskrieg: Ukraine soll bei Nato-Gipfel Milliarden bekommen
spiegel.description: Die von Russland angegriffene Ukraine soll in Ankara ein neues Versprechen für Militärhilfen erhalten. Jeweils 70 Milliarden Euro sollen in diesem und im kommenden Jahr fließen.

spiegel.title: Auswärtiges Amt zitiert Botschafter der Volksrepublik China zum Gespräch wegen Chinas Zusammenarbeit mit Russland
spiegel.description: Das Auswärtige Amt bittet Chinas Vertreter in Berlin zu einem »dringenden Gespräch«. Thema waren nach SPIEGEL-Informationen Berichte, wonach das chinesische Militär russische Soldaten ausbildet.

spiegel.title: Dieter Nuhr: 325 Beschwerden nach Witz über Frauenmorde im RBB
spiegel.description: Dieter Nuhr löste mit einem Monolog über Femizide und strukturelle Gewalt Kritik aus. Beim RBB gehen Beschwerden ein, im Rundfunkrat wird kontrovers diskutiert. Die Intendantin aber verteidigt den Kabarettisten.

spiegel.title: Volkswagen und Mercedes: Autobauer stellen Werke und Arbeitszeit infrage
spiegel.description: In der deutschen Automobilindustrie fallen die letzten Tabus: Volkswagen will vier Werke loswerden, Mercedes die 40-Stunden-Woche zurück. Die Gewerkschaften geraten in Rückzugsgefechte, die sie kaum gewinnen können.

spiegel.title: Japanische Bürgermeisterin kündigt Babypause an – und das ganze Land diskutiert
spiegel.description: Mit ihrem Mutterschutz schreibt Japans Bürgermeisterin Shoko Kawata Geschichte. Doch statt Glückwünschen bekommt die 35-Jährige eine hitzige Debatte darüber, ob gewählte Politikerinnen sich eine Babypause leisten dürfen.

spiegel.title: Capital Bra über seine Drogensucht: Was er statt der Haftbefehl-Doku schaut
spiegel.description: Vladyslav Balovatsky, alias Capital Bra, ist abhängig von Tilidin. Er hat etliche Entzugsversuche unternommen. Hier erzählt er, warum er die Netflix-Doku über den Rapper Haftbefehl nicht schauen kann und was er stattdessen guckt.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 News heute: »JUR THE MAN!« – Das sagt die Presse zum möglichen Nagelsmann-Nachfolger Jürgen Klopp
spiegel.description: Julian Nagelsmann ist nicht mehr Bundestrainer der Nationalelf, die internationale Presse blickt bereits in die Zukunft. Und: Norweger benennen Baby nach Star Haaland. Alles Wichtige zum WM-Tag 23.

spiegel.title: England: Gesundheitsdienst NHS will Menschen für Bewegung belohnen
spiegel.description: Heute schon spaziert? Für eine halbe Stunde täglich sollen Engländerinnen und Engländer künftig Gutscheine und Rabatte bekommen. Der Gesundheitsdienst NHS hofft auf ein erfolgreiches Rezept gegen Bewegungsmangel.

new-sci.description: Brain recordings from newborns reveal the first neural evidence that humans are born with an innate sense of numbers

phys-org.title: Study demonstrates neurotransmitter communication in immune cells directly for the first time
phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of Münster and Ruhr University Bochum have demonstrated for the first time in real time that the body's own defense cells use catecholamines—neurotransmitters such as dopamine and adrenaline—to communicate via the same chemical signals as nerve cells. This discovery opens up a new understanding of how the immune system is regulated. The study has been published in Advanced Science.

phys-org.title: How transformative competencies can be integrated into existing degree programs
phys-org.description: Enabling people to reflect critically on societal changes and participate in meeting major challenges is the purpose of teaching transformative competencies. phys-org.title: Fighting an emerging threat to strawberry crops
phys-org.description: A few years ago, Austin Wrenn noticed something unsettling in his strawberry greenhouses at Wrenn's Farm in Zebulon, North Carolina. He was one of the first growers in the state to experience losses from an unexpected, aggressive fungal pathogen known as Neopestalotiopsis, or Neo-P.

phys-org.title: Natural born killers—tracking immune cells as they cluster around cancer
phys-org.description: There is a constant war going on in your body. Working against you are viruses and cancer cells growing uncontrollably, threatening your tissues and organs. Fighting on your side are immune cells such as lymphocytes, a type of white blood cell that includes T cells and B cells. B cells produce antibodies that target viruses, while T cells coordinate immune responses and can kill infected or abnormal cells. Together, these defenses help limit infection and the spread of cancer.

phys-org.title: The discovery of an ancient child's skull sheds light on the early prehistoric farmers of Norway
phys-org.description: Researchers from the University of Bergen have uncovered the remains of a 4,000-year-old child in a cave site on Norway's west coast. "The find offers rare and important insight into the first agricultural population in Norway, and we hope that analysis of the bone material will help us understand what these people looked like and where they originated," says Knut Andreas Bergsvik, professor of archaeology at the University Museum of Bergen and project leader of the INDICAVE research projec

phys-org.title: How a new fungal genome-editing tool could open fresh paths to cancer treatments
phys-org.description: Researchers have spent decades—and billions of dollars—sequencing animal and crop genomes, but fungi have historically been the forgotten middle child of genomics, only noticed when they're ruining bread or colonizing toes.

phys-org.title: NASA's Hubble spots star-spangled cosmic scene
phys-org.description: More than 500,000 stars blaze red, white, and blue in this image from NASA's Hubble Space Telescope, released in celebration of the United States' 250th anniversary. The image showcases Messier 3 (M3), one of the Milky Way galaxy's most massive globular clusters, or spherical collections of gravitationally bound stars. Globular clusters are made up of ancient stars that formed at roughly the same time from the same cloud of gas, giving those stars similar ages. Around 150 known gl

phys-org.title: Visual map of 20,000 words reveals why lip-readers confuse common look-alikes
phys-org.description: New research from the University of Kansas uses network science to determine why people make mistakes when lip-reading. Michael Vitevitch, professor of speech-language-hearing at KU, and his co-authors created a visual map of about 20,000 words in English, hoping to better grasp why some words are more difficult to lip-read than others.

phys-org.title: Escaped flowerhorn fish threaten biodiversity, pose potential public health risks in Laguna, Philippines
phys-org.description: A hardy aquarium fish prized for its golden hue, the ornamental Flowerhorn cichlid (Amphilophus spp.) has become a problem for the residents of San Pablo City, Laguna: It is increasingly taking on an outsized role in both the natural ecosystem and local aquaculture operations in nearby Lake Sampaloc.

phys-org.title: Cosmic neutrino 'whispers' may surface in 5,000-day Super-Kamiokande signal
phys-org.description: Neutrinos: They have no electric charge, pass through matter like a ghost and are so light they were initially thought to have zero mass. These are just some of the traits that make them so difficult to detect. Research on neutrinos requires massive underground observatories far from potential confounders that drown out their weak signals. One of the largest in the world, located 1,000 meters (3,281 feet) underground in Gifu Prefecture, Japan, is called Super-Kamiokande.

phys-org.title: Sea turtles diving through the eye of the storm help develop better cyclone forecasts
phys-org.description: Every summer, communities across northern Australia brace for the tropical cyclone season. Tropical cyclones draw their power from the warm seas, extracting heat and moisture from ocean water.

phys-org.title: Beachcomber's find fuels whale study breakthrough
phys-org.description: During his morning runs, Rod Keogh had no doubt that the whale poo he saw washed up on the beach had value. Science has finally caught up with him. Samples collected by the South Australian man have contributed to a groundbreaking study of the diets and microbiomes of southern right whales, led by Macquarie University in Sydney and Waipapa Taumata Rau, University of Auckland. The study is now published in the journal Molecular Ecology.

phys-org.title: Climate change will raise the risk of severe heat waves: New Zealand homes aren't ready
phys-org.description: Europe's summer heat wave has exposed tens of millions of people to temperatures above 35°C, broken records and claimed hundreds of lives. Early climate attribution studies suggest Europe's event would have been "virtually impossible" just 50 years ago without human-caused climate change.

phys-org.title: The founding father of American literature, Charles Brockden Brown saw his nation's dark side
phys-org.description: Murder, suicide, spontaneous combustion, sleepwalking, ventriloquism: These are some of the sensational events in the novels of Charles Brockden Brown (1771–1810). As the United States' first professional author, Brown is the Founding Father of the nation's literature. He is, according to one biographer, "the most important American author no one has ever heard of." His fiction was deeply engaged with politics and culture after the American Revolution.

phys-org.title: Songs play a greater role than plumage color in limiting bird hybridization, study suggests
phys-org.description: When trying to attract and recognize potential mates, animals are known to rely on various signals, traits and behaviors. In the case of birds, these signals can typically include a wide range of sounds—such as trills, whistles, chirps or melodious notes defined as "songs"—as well as the color and movement of their feathers.

phys-org.title: Could this asteroid be a piece of the moon? A Chinese spacecraft is about to find out
phys-org.description: The moon is not the only natural object traveling through space alongside Earth. Several small asteroids travel around the sun in near lockstep with our planet. And just like Earth, these space rocks also take a year to complete a full orbit. Today, we know of eight such "quasi-moons" or quasi-satellites.

phys-org.title: Projected 'super typhoon' heads for US Pacific islands
phys-org.description: Residents of Guam and the Northern Marianas boarded up windows and stocked up Friday as a monster weather system forecast to become a "super typhoon" approached the U.S. Pacific territories.

phys-org.title: France deaths rose by 30% during heatwave
phys-org.description: France endured a rise of nearly 30% in the number of deaths recorded during the week starting June 22, the peak of a record-breaking heat wave that battered the country, the public health authority said Friday.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

proj-syn.description: If Ukraine can continue to disrupt Crimea, strike more targets in the heart of Russia, frustrate Russia’s frontline forces, and pile more pressure on Russia’s hobbled economy, President Vladimir Putin will feel increasingly cornered. proj-syn.description: Without a EU-level framework capable of turning resources into scale, the bloc’s defense capabilities will remain limited, no matter how much member countries spends. proj-syn.title: From the American Revolution to Universal Suffrage
proj-syn.description: Britain’s attempt to crush the American Revolution exposed a constitutional crisis at the heart of its empire. One English statesman saw in it proof that only broader suffrage could check royal power, tame corruption, and ensure that imperial rule remained compatible with liberty.

proj-syn.title: 250 Years of American State Capitalism
proj-syn.description: While the prevailing economic narrative in the United States has often extolled free markets, policymaking itself has always been more pragmatic. From its very founding, the US has had a hybrid model in which the state directs, subsidizes, and occasionally bails out private enterprise in the service of national priorities.

proj-syn.title: Three Essentials of a More Equal World Order
proj-syn.description: A growing awareness of the inequities embedded in the world order has prompted calls for reform. Building a multilateral system that serves the global majority will require redesigning the international financial architecture, especially in relation to sovereign debt and corporate taxation.

proj-syn.title: The US as the World’s Robber Baron
proj-syn.description: Like the Gilded Age robber barons, the United States under President Donald Trump is using trade policy to benefit itself at the expense of all other countries. But now that administration surrogates are openly acknowledging the strategy, all other major trading powers will surely respond accordingly.

proj-syn.title: A Democratic Opening for Azerbaijan
proj-syn.description: With Armenia's recent elections likely to usher in an era of greater stability—and less Russian influence—in the South Caucasus, neighboring Azerbaijan is well-positioned to deepen cooperation with the US and Europe. But without appropriate conditions, new strategic partnerships with the West could fail to deliver for Azerbaijanis.

proj-syn.title: The Mismeasure of Europe’s Economy
